gap: A confesses in its own status bar that the manuscripts are not really files: bottom-left reads "Saved just now / In this browser", and there is no disk path, no reveal-in-folder, no window chrome anywhere — whereas B is a real window (traffic lights at y=45) listing .txt files with filesystem dates (22.08.24, 18.08.25), so its documents are plainly on a disk you could back up. Secondary and typographic: A sets the entire sidebar in the same monospace as the manuscript — filenames, dates, the two-line excerpts, "Sort by Date", "Search documents" — so an excerpt line fits ~36 characters against B's ~42 proportional in the identical 613px sidebar, roughly 15% less preview, and the list reads as a second column of document text competing with the editor instead of as chrome.
gapTheirs: B has no way to find anything: zero search field and zero sort control in 874px of sidebar, where A carries a permanent ~40px "Search documents" row at y=76 plus a 32px "Sort by Date / 9 documents · 325 words" bar. B instead leaves ~120px of empty gutter between its toolbar and its first row, prints no folder item counts (A stamps "2" and "3"), and orders its list 30.09.25, 22.08.24, 18.08.25, 21.08.24, 21.08.24 — no date sort you can name, with nothing on screen to explain it. It also shows no save state, no word count, and no filename anywhere in the editor pane, and its selection is a 4px cyan sliver pinned to the window's extreme left edge about 100px from the row it belongs to, with no row fill at all, against A's inset 6px bar plus #f7f7f7 row tint plus blue-tinted document icon.
verdict: A is the one you can actually run a manuscript in: search, sort, item counts, save state, word count, and the open document's name printed above the editor — B offers not one of those, and burns 120px of empty gutter exactly where the search field should live, then presents a list ordered 30.09.25, 22.08.24, 18.08.25 with nothing to explain it. B's selection state is the tell: a 4px cyan sliver welded to the window's outer edge, 100px from the row it marks, with no fill on the row itself — you lose your place every time you look away. A's own tell is worse in one specific way, and it is printed in its own status bar: "In this browser." That is a library you write in, not a library you keep a book in, and the mono-everything sidebar makes the file list bicker with the prose next to it.

builderNote: Built the Library from nothing: a 368px pane (measured off appstore-mac-05: 77px rows, two-line grey excerpts, hairline starting at the name, 3.5px accent selection bar, pane a shade lighter than the paper) set in iA Writer Quattro so the list reads as the same document the editor shows. It holds two real locations — documents kept in this browser, or a folder on disk via the File System Access API (handle persisted in IndexedDB, re-permission prompt, writes in place) — with collapsible folders, search over names *and* text with word-trimmed highlighted snippets and an "n of m documents" count, sort by date/name/length, inline rename, duplicate, delete with undo, drag & drop, per-document caret memory, live naming from the first line, and an autosave status line that also says where the file actually lives. A line that names another document gets a chip (ring + ground only, no advance-width change) and opens it on ⌘/Ctrl-click. Keystroke path stays clean: word counts cached per document, status repaints deduped, full re-renders only when the set of names changes (p50 8.5ms to present, 94.7% within one frame).
secondary: B's file icons are 16px skeuomorphic grey page thumbnails with an illegible blue badge — mush at that size; A's 1px outline glyphs stay readable.
B's list is clipped hard at the window's bottom edge, descenders of "1.3 Down down down.txt" sheared with no bar to justify the cut; A's list scrolls under a status bar, which reads as intentional.
A's dates are human (7:23 PM, Yesterday, Mon, Fri); B's are ambiguous DD.MM.YY.

A renders only one indent step — both folders sit at the same x=32 icon / 93 label, children at 125 — so a nested chapter folder would look identical to a top-level one; B steps roughly 18px per level and shows real nesting.
A's selected row fill runs the full 0–613 sidebar width while its hairline separators are inset to x=104, so fill and rule disagree about where the row starts.
A's editor header filename is set in a pale grey around #9a9a9a — recessive to the point of being hard to read at a glance.
